OpenSearch with user OAuth tokens

Source: vignettes/opensearch.Rmd
opensearch.Rmd

OpenSearch is an open-source search and analytics engine. It stores documents in indexes and can search them or query them with its SQL plugin. Use oauth_db_opensearch_api() to search OpenSearch with each Shiny visitor’s current OAuth access token. It supports Query DSL, aggregations and the SQL plugin through HTTPS. You do not need an OpenSearch R driver or JDBC.

Try OpenSearch locally

Start Docker and run:

shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("opensearch")

The package starts OpenSearch 3.9.0 with its Security plugin, Keycloak and a Shiny app. Alice and Bob see their own documents, and Try a write shows that their roles cannot change the index. See Local Docker demos for accounts and cleanup; allow at least 2 GB of Docker memory for OpenSearch.

oauth_db_demo("opensearch", action = "files") copies the configuration. opensearch/prepare.py creates the signing-key, role and document-permission settings; realm-extended.json configures the corresponding Shiny client. The signing key is a startup snapshot. For rotating keys, use the OIDC authenticator described later in this guide.

Settings for the example

The cluster needs the Security plugin, HTTPS and bearer-token authentication. Its OIDC/JWT and role configuration follow the app example.

Setting Where to get it
url The cluster’s HTTPS API endpoint, rather than the Dashboards page
Index, such as orders OpenSearch Dashboards’ index list or your administrator
Issuer, client ID, secret The Shiny registration with the cluster’s trusted provider
search.read The example API scope; define it in your provider or use your deployment’s scope

Save OAUTHDB_OPENSEARCH_ISSUER, OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID and OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET in .Renviron, then restart R. AWS endpoints that require SigV4 need a different client.

A complete app

Replace the cluster URL and index name. This example assumes the provider exposes a search.read scope; use your own registration’s scopes.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_OPENSEARCH_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "search.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    verbatimTextOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  search <- oauth_db_opensearch_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = "https://search.example.org",
    required_scopes = "search.read"
  )
  output$rows <- renderPrint({
    result <- search$search(
      "orders",
      body = list(
        size = 20L,
        query = list(term = list(country = "NL"))
      )
    )
    result$hits
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R"). The app waits for sign-in before making requests and clears the output on sign-out. If your provider requires a resource parameter or named token target, configure it in shinyOAuth and pass the target name to the helper’s target argument.

Configure cluster authentication and permissions

Enable the Security plugin and configure its OpenID Connect authentication or JWT authentication. The cluster must accept the access tokens issued to your Shiny client, validate their issuer and audience, and map their subject and backend roles to OpenSearch roles. Enable HTTPS with a trusted certificate.

For JWT authentication, the relevant HTTP authentication settings are:

jwt_auth_domain:
  http_enabled: true
  transport_enabled: false
  order: 0
  http_authenticator:
    type: jwt
    challenge: false
    config:
      jwt_header: Authorization
      jwt_url_parameter: null
      subject_key: sub
      roles_key: roles
      required_issuer: https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
      required_audience: opensearch-reporting
      signing_key: |
        -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
        Replace with the trusted issuer's public signing key.
        -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
  authentication_backend:
    type: noop

This is a configuration fragment, with a placeholder key. Add it to the cluster’s HTTP authentication configuration using the Security plugin’s administration procedure. For discovery and rotating signing keys, configure the OIDC authenticator instead of copying this static-key example.

Map the provider’s role claims to roles granting access to the required indexes and operations. OpenSearch document-level and field-level security can further limit which documents and fields each visitor receives. The helper forwards the token; the server makes these decisions. A login to OpenSearch Dashboards alone does not establish API access.

The endpoint must accept OAuth bearer tokens. AWS IAM/SigV4 authentication requires a different client; this helper does not sign AWS requests.

Register the Shiny client

Register an OAuth client with the trusted identity provider. Allow http://localhost:8100 as its redirect URI and request an access token for the audience configured on OpenSearch. Configure any role claims the cluster requires. Request your provider’s scopes, including offline_access if it requires that scope for renewal.

Save the registration in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_OPENSEARCH_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting

Search results and aggregations

Results retain their native structure: result$hits$hits contains documents and metadata, result$hits$total contains the total and its relation, and result$aggregations contains aggregation results. Arrays stay lists and large JSON integers remain strings. This avoids flattening nested documents or losing precision. Select the fields you need when building a table.

An empty body = list() becomes {}. Use named R lists for JSON objects and unnamed lists for JSON arrays, including single-element arrays. For a nested empty JSON object, use structure(list(), names = character()).

result <- search$search(
  "orders",
  body = list(
    size = 0L,
    aggs = list(countries = list(terms = list(field = "country")))
  )
)
result$aggregations$countries$buckets

An index can be a pattern or a vector such as c("orders-*", "archive"). Omitting it uses the cluster-wide endpoint; permissions may reject searches spanning restricted indexes. Paginate explicitly with from/size, or a stable sort and search_after. The helper never fetches additional pages automatically. Searches reporting a timeout or failed shards raise an error. Use raw = TRUE to inspect their native response, or $request() for responses reduced with filter_path.

SQL and native JSON requests

SQL requires the server’s SQL plugin and permissions for its APIs, index reads and required index metadata. The response preserves schema, datarows, totals and any cursor, using the plugin’s JDBC JSON format:

page <- search$sql(
  "SELECT owner, total FROM orders WHERE country = ?",
  parameters = list(list(type = "keyword", value = "NL"))
)
page$schema
page$datarows

Parameters use the plugin’s native typed descriptors and ? placeholders; values are not interpolated into SQL. Dates and other values requiring a specific representation should be encoded according to the server’s type.

Use $request() for other JSON APIs. For example, a paginated SQL request uses list(query = "SELECT owner FROM orders", fetch_size = 20L) as its body, followed by list(cursor = page$cursor) to obtain another page from the same SQL endpoint. Close an unfinished cursor by posting its value to c("_plugins", "_sql", "close"). Consume or close cursors before switching accounts; the client does not store cursor state or close server resources automatically. Bulk NDJSON needs a separate native client.

Tokens, errors and TLS

Each operation obtains a current token and checks the authorization again after the response arrives. Responses from an ended or replaced authorization are discarded. GET and HEAD may renew once after HTTP 401; POST searches, SQL, writes and other mutations are never replayed. A timeout or sign-out stops local access; submitted work can continue on the server.

HTTP errors report a status and safe diagnostics without echoing response bodies or credentials. raw = TRUE returns an httr2 response for successful requests. Use it with httr2 response helpers when inspecting native JSON.

Pass ca_bundle = "path/to/private-ca.pem" for a private CA. On Windows, if the default Schannel curl backend does not accept your PEM CA bundle, set CURL_SSL_BACKEND=openssl in .Renviron and restart R before loading the package. Certificate and hostname verification remain enabled.

The source checkout’s OpenSearch OAuth fixture tests real signed JWTs, document and field permissions, SQL and TLS. With Docker and the R test dependencies installed, run Rscript --vanilla tools/check-opensearch-oauth.R from the repository root. It creates its own certificates and tokens; no production credentials are used.
